theorem twoDimensionalAncientAndShrinkingSolitonClassification
    (P : TwoDimensionalClassificationPredecessors (M := M)) :
    TwoDimensionalClassificationTheory (M := M) := by
  refine {
    asymptotic_round := P.asymptoticRoundTheory
    shrinking_soliton := exists_twoDimensionalShrinkingSolitonConclusion
    ancient_classification := ?_ }
  intro K
  have hsequence : Nonempty (AncientRescalingSequence K) :=
    K.exists_ancientRescalingSequence
  obtain ⟨S⟩ := hsequence
  exact ⟨P.ancientRoundCertificate_of_sequence K S⟩

tex_content.label: thm:surface-ancient
tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Ancient surface solutions] Every two-dimensional ancient $\kappa $-solution is compact and has constant positive sectional curvature on each slice, including time zero. Every two-dimensional asymptotic limit of Theorem 2 is compact and round at every negative time.

↗ lem:surface-shrinker ↗ thm:ancient-asymptotic Source: MT2007, ChowKnopf2004 1. Morgan–Tian, Corollaries 9.49–9.50, pp. 213–2142. Chow–Knopf, Lemma 5.38 and Proposition 5.39, pp. 133–134
Proof

The surface-shrinker lemma makes each asymptotic slice compact and round. Exhaustion embeddings from the compact limit eventually cover the original connected surface, so they are global diffeomorphisms. Scalar positivity allows the entropy identity; its backward limit is the round entropy. Equality in its monotonicity forces roundness of the original flow at every negative time, and smooth continuity includes time zero.

□
